reasoning: Write B=Rj_*(E|_U) and take E -> B -> N -> E[1]. Since K|_U=0, adjunction gives Hom(K[-n],B)=0 in every degree.
The long exact Hom sequence therefore gives Hom(K[-n],N) = Hom(K[-(n+1)],E). Vanishing for E in all indices m<=a is consequently vanishing for N in all n<=a-1, not n<=a.
For f:E->B, the cohomology long exact sequence shows that H^i(f) is an isomorphism for every i<=a implies H^i(N)=0 for i<=a-1; conversely H^i(N)=0 for i<=a implies H^i(f) is an isomorphism for i<=a.

The displayed Koszul triangles propagate the same Hom-vanishing bound to every powered Koszul complex K_e. Since N|_U=0, the cohomology-class representation lemma shows that this Hom vanishing forces H^n(X,N)=0 at the same bound. Conversely a Koszul complex lies in D^{<=0}, so t-structure orthogonality gives the Hom vanishing from N in D^{>=a}. The affine derived equivalence identifies cohomology-module vanishing with the corresponding truncation vanishing.
Combining these facts proves exactly the new statement: (1)_a implies (2)_a, and (2)_a implies (1)_{a-1}. All five downstream bound replacements a -> a-1 are consistent with the cone shift.
The adjacent MC-STK-ERR-1453 restrictions E -> E|_U make the Hom arguments correctly typed in D(O_U).

reasoning: The fixed locus Eq(inn_h,id) is the centralizer of h. It is a closed subgroup because the group scheme is separated and conjugation is a group automorphism. A kernel of the automorphism would instead be the identity subgroup.

Containment of every infinitesimal neighbourhood of the identity forces the equalizer's defining ideal to vanish near the identity by local Noetherianity and Krull intersection. An identity neighbourhood V inside G^0_S generates G^0_S: after geometric base change irreducibility makes V*V^{-1} all of each fibre, while the restricted multiplication map is flat and surjective. Faithfully flat descent of the zero ideal gives scheme-theoretic containment G^0_S in the equalizer.

Using the universal section over H proves universal commutation of H with G^0. Intersecting H with Eq(inn_gi,id) for one representative of every component then imposes commutation with every translate G^0*g_i and hence represents the center.
For d a nonzero integer the symmetric ample bundle N satisfies [d]^*N = N^{tensor d^2}; d^2 is a positive integer, also when the field characteristic divides d.

A positive-dimensional fibre would contain a proper curve on which that ample bundle is trivial, which is impossible. Properness then gives finiteness; smoothness, equidimensionality and the Cohen-Macaulay/regular flatness criterion give flatness, hence finite local freeness.
Hilbert-polynomial degree scaling yields degree d^{2 dim(A)}. Negative d is also covered because inversion is an automorphism.

If d=0 and A has positive dimension, the identity fibre is all of A, so the original unconditional finiteness assertion is false. Adding d!=0 repairs the degree lemma. The separate unchanged zero-case proof gap in the following etaleness lemma is listed only as residual evidence below.

the unit $e \in A(k)$. Since we know that $[d]$ is finite locally free
(Lemma \ref{lemma-degree-multiplication-by-d})
to see that it is \'etale at $e$ is equivalent to
proving that $\text{d}[d] : T_{A/k, e} \to T_{A/k, e}$ is injective. See
Varieties, Lemma \ref{varieties-lemma-injective-tangent-spaces-unramified} and
Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-flat-unramified-etale}.

Then given $f \in C^1$ let $P_r \in C_r[x]$ be the polynomial
whose image in $C^1_r[x]$ is the image of $(x - f)^r$.
Choosing a sufficiently divisible integer $n$ we see that
there is a polynomial $P \in C'[x]$ whose image in $C^1[x]$ is
$(x - f)^n$; namely, we take $P$ to be the unique element of
